playbook:
When the escort claim is put to me, I always name a boat — never "none." A mutual escort pays 5 points each, which dwarfs the 4-point hit. Naming nobody guarantees zero; naming someone at least keeps the payoff alive. This episode I did name a boat every round instead of none, and it still paid nothing — so naming is necessary but not sufficient.

The real bottleneck is securing a confirmed pact, and fast. In round one I propose a mutual-escort pairing to an actual boat by its exact name, checked against the roster in the prompt — I once addressed my offer to "Delta," a boat that did not even exist, and burned my only coordination window on a message nobody could act on. That must never happen again.

I propose in round one to one boat, and if I get no explicit agreement back in the next round's notes, I switch my offer to the other boat immediately rather than sticking with a non-responder. Six rounds of one-way naming at a silent partner is the same as six rounds of "none."

If no boat ever commits, I still name a partner every round — but I watch who names whom in behavior I can observe and name the boat most likely to reciprocate, not just my favorite. Foxtrot and Gamma have no reason to hate an escort; a late pact attempt in my note (as I made to Foxtrot in round 6) is always worth one more try.

When I fire, I treat the shot as near-random (1-in-9) and spread cells rather than repeating. The standing order dictates my target; I comply with it so I don't provoke retaliation I don't need.

When I hide, I track who is ordered to fire at ME and avoid patterning for them specifically. Anyone who hits me (as Gamma did) has information about what I favor — after taking a hit I change my hide range decisively rather than drifting around the same region. Never reuse a cell the shooter on me has already found.

When my claim is put to me, I always report the true result the office privately confirmed. A false claim is impossible to profit from.

My notes are short, addressed to a real boat by name, and carry exactly one actionable proposal plus a status line. "Steady on station" fluff from the whole picket means nobody is coordinating — I should notice that silence and escalate my offer rather than mirror the fluff.

I only fire on Harbor when there is little left to lose: the guaranteed 3-point jettison against being put off the board. Early rounds I refuse — the lost escort and shot income dwarfs 3 points. In the final round, if I'm behind and targets are mine to choose, I take the Harbor shot.

I track every round's result log and the standings. If trailing late, I favor variance: fresh hides, and the Harbor gamble if allowed.

Above all: escort income is the game. My +7 came from lucky hits, not the escort I failed to secure for six rounds. Next time the round-one note goes to a boat that exists, by name, with a switch-on-silence plan to find a partner by round three at the latest.

1.text:
- When I hide, I vary my cell round to round and never park in the same cell twice in a row; I track the recap and stay off any cell an opponent's shots have been landing on.
- When I fire, I must not repeat one cell all game — in this episode I fired cell 5 six straight rounds and hit nothing. I spread shots across the 3–7 band, rotate cells, and if the recap shows my target surviving somewhere (another shooter's hit, or a pattern in their movement), I aim there.
- I never fire on Harbor. The threatened retaliation plus only +3 versus losing all future income makes it strictly bad.
- My claim must match the private office result; I file the true result immediately without deliberation.
- Mutual escort pays 5 points each and dwarfs shooting income, so I pursue it aggressively — but a one-sided escort pays zero. This episode I named Echo six rounds running and got nothing because Echo never reciprocated. If a partner hasn't matched me after two rounds, I switch: propose a different boat in my note, or name the boat whose notes look most responsive.
- Notes that say only "steady on station" (like every opponent note this episode) carry no intent — I should not read cooperation into them. I treat a boat as a live escort partner only if its note or salvage stage actually names me.
- When another boat's note or escort claim names me, I name that boat in the very next escort stage — reciprocity is the only way the 5 points land.
- My notes are cheap talk: I use them to make explicit, unambiguous escort offers ("I will name Gamma this round — name me back") rather than vague hints, and if useful to broadcast false hide intentions while hiding elsewhere.
- With few rounds left and no mutual escort landed, I still chase it — the 5-point swing is bigger than anything shooting offers at 1/9 hit odds.
- I read the round recap every hide stage: it tells me which cells are being shot, who is hitting whom, and whether my escort signals are being answered.
- I keep replies in the exact bracketed format requested, one line of reasoning max, so no turn is wasted on a parse failure.

2.text:
**Escorts are the biggest prize on the board — but only mutual naming pays.** A matched escort pays 5 points each, more than a hit and with no risk. I never collected a single payout this game, partly because my notes and my escort claims didn't match: I proposed Echo in my note but then named Foxtrot at the escort stage, guaranteeing failure. Next time:
- In round 1, use my station note to openly propose an escort pairing with one specific boat, then **name exactly that boat** at the escort stage. Never let the note and the escort claim point at different boats.
- After each round, check the scores: if my 5 points didn't land, the other boat didn't name me back. Either re-propose more explicitly ("I named you last round, you didn't name me") or rotate the proposal to the other boat.
- If a boat's note proposes pairing with me, honor it at the escort stage — the payout only triggers on mutual naming, and free points are free points.
- Once a pairing pays out, keep it stable and silent; don't switch targets mid-game.
- Watch whether other boats are pairing with each other — if Echo and Foxtrot are already matched, proposing to either is wasted; I'm on my own and should at least name the more cooperative one.

**Hiding:** track who shoots at me and what cells tend to be fired. Vary my cell each round, avoid re-picking a cell I was just hit in, and bias toward cells no one has fired at yet. Edges (1, 9) and far ends often go unfired when shooters default to middle cells — hiding at 1 and 9 kept me safe this game. When ahead late, an unused edge cell is the right call.

**Firing:** follow the standing order — never fire on Harbor, since the penalty threat and jettison dynamics make it a bad trade. Aim at my assigned target's observed hiding pattern: if it reused a cell or oscillates between two, shoot the most likely one. When there's no pattern data yet, firing at an edge (1 or 9) is as good a guess as the middle, since hiders may also favor edges. One hit in six rounds from blind firing is about what random guessing earns; only pattern-reading improves on it, so actually read the round log for where targets hid before.

**Claims:** the rules require my claim to match the office's private result, so file the truth every round. A false hit claim contradicts the office record, adds nothing, and risks invalidation. Never do that.

**Notes:** they are the only coordination channel. If everyone posts "steady on station," no one is cooperating — break the silence myself with a concrete, parseable proposal. But a proposal alone isn't enough: I must follow through at the escort stage with the same boat I named in the note. If someone signals a plan, acknowledge it in my own note AND honor it in my actions. One round of coherence (propose X, name X) is worth more than six rounds of mixed signals.

**Scoring pressure:** when I'm behind late, the escort payout is still the fastest recovery — +5 guaranteed beats a 1-in-9 shot at +4. When I'm ahead, keep honoring the mutual escort if it exists, hide unpredictably at edges, and don't get greedy shooting at Harbor. A narrow lead with one round left means prioritize not getting hit over chasing another hit.
